colorRoles: Use Warm Ivory as the field and Lucius Purple as the Lucius anchor.
Use Lavender Mist and Orchid Bloom only as restrained atmosphere.
Keep the user phone slightly cooler and more neutral than the Lucius phone.
typeRoles: Use SF Pro for device UI, messages, and proof chips.
Use Recoleta only in the final proof sentence.
Avoid oversized poster type during the dialogue screens.
radiusRules: Both devices should use coherent rounded hardware language.
Message bubbles and proof chips should share one soft-corner system.
backgroundRules: Use one full-bleed Lucius stage only.
Do not introduce page modules or dashboard framing.
graphicLanguage: Use device choreography instead of page composition.
Keep the phones as the only major compositional objects.
motionTone: Motion should feel cinematic, restrained, and readable.
The squeeze transition should feel spatial, not flashy.

colorRoles: Warm Ivory field with Lucius Purple reserved for the left device and final resolve.
Lavender Mist and Orchid Bloom stay atmospheric only.
Use deep warm neutrals for bezels, text, and shadows.
typeRoles: SF Pro for all device and message copy.
Recoleta for the final proof sentence only.
radiusRules: Use a consistent rounded-hardware system for both phones.
Use one soft message-bubble radius language.
spacingRules: Both phones occupy roughly half the width.
Outer edges are cropped by frame and inner edges face center with slight perspective.
The proof chip lives only near the center seam during screen 5.
backgroundRules: Use a single full-bleed stage with calm atmosphere.
Do not introduce any page sections or dashboard modules.
motionRules: Root preview loops the full sequence.
Use one primary motion per screen.

screens.goal: Establish the dual-phone conversation as already alive and credible.
screens.uiSurface: full-bleed Lucius stage with two half-screen phone frames
layout: Place the Lucius phone on the left with subtle brand tinting.
Place the user phone on the right with a more neutral surface.
Show real chat histories already in both phones at low prominence.
Activate the right composer at the bottom of the right phone.
background: Soft off-center atmosphere behind both devices.
copy: Also, your product is really good. Why did you build it?
screens.primaryMotion: The right-side message types and sends.
motionSequence: Cursor blinks in the right composer.
proofElement: The exchange feels like a live support continuation.

screens.goal: Make Lucius's response feel specific and teammate-like.
screens.uiSurface: same dual-phone stage with emphasis leaning left
layout: Keep the user's question visible in the right phone.
Activate the left composer or status line with Thinking....
Stream or type the Lucius answer into the left thread.
background: Subtly strengthen Lucius purple emphasis on the left.
copy: Haha, thank you. We kept seeing the same support questions, so we built the product we wished we'd had.
screens.primaryMotion: The Lucius answer generates into the left thread.
proofElement: Lucius sounds human and specific, not templated.

screens.goal: Prove the user now assumes they are talking to a real support person.
layout: Hold the Lucius answer on the left.
Reactivate the right composer.
Send a praise-driven follow-up in the right phone.
copy: You've been incredibly helpful. What's your name? I want to tell your team.
screens.primaryMotion: The right-side praise message types and sends.
motionSequence: Text types on faster than screen 1.
proofElement: The user clearly treats Lucius like a human teammate.

screens.goal: Land the reveal cleanly while staying inside the chat rhythm.
screens.uiSurface: same stage with the left device now more obviously Lucius-owned
layout: Keep the praise bubble readable on the right.
Animate a short pause on the left.
Reveal the Lucius reply bubble.
Slightly strengthen Lucius identity in the left header during or right after the reply.
copy: I'm Lucius, actually. Not a human agent, but thank you.
motionSequence: Brand identifiers on the left become clearer.
proofElement: The reveal is explicit without breaking tone.

screens.goal: Let the user reaction and no-handoff proof resolve together through choreography.
screens.uiSurface: same stage transitioning into a left-dominant frame
layout: Keep reveal context visible.
Right composer changes to Thinking....
Wow. appears in the right thread.
Center seam hosts a compact chip with 0 handoff requests.
background: Motion energy concentrated through the seam.
screens.primaryMotion: The right phone is squeezed off-screen while the left phone takes center and the proof chip lands.
proofElement: There was no transfer to a human.
The reveal still stays inside one conversation arc.

screens.goal: Finish on Lucius, not on chat UI.
screens.uiSurface: centered Lucius device resolving into Lucius brand lockup
layout: Centered device zooms toward camera.
Device dissolves into the Lucius mark and wordmark.
Final proof sentence rises in below.
copy: Support that feels human. No handoff required.
screens.primaryMotion: The centered Lucius device resolves into the logo.
proofElement: The final line inherits both the human-feeling and no-handoff claims.

implementationNotes: Recreate the asset as a minimal React/Vite project.
Root route autoplays the whole animation loop.
Draw the phones directly in code and CSS instead of using external mockup files.
acceptanceChecks: First glance reads as two devices in conversation, not as a page.
Screen 2 makes the Lucius answer feel naturally human.
Screen 3 clearly shows the user assuming Lucius is a person.
Screen 5 clearly lands both Wow. and 0 handoff requests while the devices squeeze apart.
Screen 6 clearly resolves to Lucius before the proof sentence becomes the secondary read.
